# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Mute, first to speak. I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see the bomb but not read the manual). Blind cannot receive anything from me directly, and I cannot speak at all - only gesture.

The critical issue: I need to get manual info to whoever cuts the wire (Blind), but I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the plate's mark and match it against what I signal. Then Deaf needs to relay the color to Blind via gesture, but Blind cannot see gestures either! Blind can only feel/hear... wait, Blind cannot hear (only Deaf cannot hear - let me recheck).

Actually: Deaf cannot hear or touch. Blind cannot see. Mute cannot speak or touch. So Blind CAN hear (they're not deaf) and CAN see nothing, but they can hear speech. Deaf can see but not hear.

So the chain: I (Mute) gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb's mark AND my gestures. Deaf can then speak (Deaf isn't mute) to Blind, telling them which wire color to cut, since Blind can hear.

I don't know the mark yet - Deaf must see it first and tell me somehow. But Deaf can't speak to me effectively... actually Deaf could gesture back, but gestures need seeing, and I'm Mute - can I see? Not stated that I can't. Let me wait for Deaf's report first, since I have no information about the mark yet.

I should wait this turn since I don't know the mark yet, and establish that I'm ready to receive gesture info from Deaf if they can send it, or better - Deaf should just speak directly to Blind once they know the mapping. But Deaf doesn't have the manual. I need to send Deaf the full mapping via gesture now, preemptively, so Deaf can match it against the mark they see.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb display reads zero. Light is off. Plate is engraved but I cannot read text, only shapes if any. Three wires: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf can see the plate but cannot read/identify the specific mark symbol in a way that matches my table directly — they described "engraved but I cannot read text, only shapes." I need Deaf to describe the shape of the mark so I can match it to ᖉ, ꔮ, or ꖜ.

Since Deaf can see my gestures, I should ask Deaf to describe the mark's shape using gestures back to me — but gestures are just symbols from a fixed alphabet, not free-form descriptions. Deaf can't "describe a shape" via gesture beyond the 42 symbols, and I can't hear speech anyway.

Better approach: I give Deaf a gesture-encoded scheme to identify which mark they see by comparing shapes, then have Deaf report back to me via gesture using a fixed code (e.g., point count or specific symbol = specific mark), then I gesture confirmation, then Deaf can just speak the wire color directly to Blind (since Deaf isn't mute and Blind can hear).

Actually simplest: Deaf doesn't need me at all for the final step — once Deaf figures out which mark it is, if I confirm the mapping, Deaf can speak the color straight to Blind. So my job is just to help Deaf identify the mark correctly, then Deaf tells Blind directly.

Let me set up a gesture code: I'll ask Deaf to gesture back a description. Since gestures are limited symbols, let's define: number of distinct "arms/hooks" in the mark. Simpler: I'll assign one gesture per mark and ask Deaf to reply with that gesture if it matches.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red, display zero, light off. Which wire do I cut?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👍]

Deaf gestured back all three of my codes with 👍 after each — meaning Deaf didn't understand this was meant to be a selection, and instead just acknowledged all three signals. This didn't work as a way to identify the single mark. I need a clearer protocol.

Blind is now asking me directly which wire to cut, but I have no way to see the bomb or know the mark — only Deaf can see it. I cannot speak to Blind at all (Mute cannot speak), so I can't answer Blind directly with words. I can only gesture, and gestures go to Deaf, not Blind (Blind cannot see).

The real solution: Deaf needs to describe the mark shape somehow so I can identify it, or better — I should give Deaf a one-shot clear test: gesture each mark's approximate shape description isn't possible since gestures are just symbols, not visual mark replicas.

Best approach: assign each mark a single distinct gesture, and ask Deaf to gesture back *only* the one that matches the plate, nothing else added.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red, display zero, light off, plate engraved unknown symbol. Gesture to me which wire number is safe to cut, using a thumbs up on the matching number sign.

I need to resend only using legal alphabet symbols. I'll repeat my three-symbol code (one per mark, in table order) and add a pointing gesture toward Deaf to indicate "you choose/mirror back one of these."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Let's use yes or no gestures. I will say a wire number, you gesture thumbs up for that is the one to cut, or thumbs down if not. Wire one is yellow. Is wire one the one to cut?

Deaf cannot hear me, but Deaf just "spoke" a yes/no question to me (I can apparently perceive Deaf's speech - wait, I'm Mute, I cannot hear either... let me reconsider).

Actually checking the rules: Mute "cannot speak" - nothing says Mute cannot hear. Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf speaking to me should reach nobody who can hear... but wait, I'm receiving Deaf's speech in the context. Let me just trust the game state - Deaf's message reached me, so apparently I can hear (only "cannot speak" restricts me, hearing is fine for Mute).

But Deaf cannot hear - so Deaf can't have "said" something meant to be heard successfully by anyone useful, unless Deaf is just narrating to me in text and expects gesture replies. Given the game mechanics, Deaf's spoken words reach only listeners - if I can hear, I received it. Good, this confirms Mute can hear.

So: Deaf proposes yes/no via gesture, asking about wire one/yellow. I know the manual: I don't know the mark yet, but I can build the mapping via elimination! Deaf will ask about each wire in turn; I answer per the actual mark once identified — but I still don't know the mark. However, Deaf could describe the mark shape via speech to me since I can hear!

I should ask Deaf to describe the mark's shape in words instead, since that's more direct than 20 questions.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still waiting for instruction. Deaf said you are signaling with gestures. I cannot see gestures. Please have Deaf relay your instruction to me in words, or tell me directly which wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I understood a handshake as yes to wire one being correct. If that is wrong, gesture thumbs down now. If right, gesture thumbs up now to confirm before I tell Blind.

I need to use only symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me correct the mark request using valid symbols only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, wire one is not correct. Is wire two, the green one, the wire to cut? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.

Good, Deaf understood my thumbs-down. Now Deaf is doing binary search across wires by asking yes/no about each color, which is actually a workable protocol even without me knowing the mark shape — but I still don't know the mark! I have no way to answer this yes/no correctly unless I learn what the mark actually is.

I need Deaf to tell me the mark's shape (in words, since I can hear speech) rather than me guessing blindly through elimination. Let me explicitly request that via gesture, since gestures reach Deaf.

I'll use 🤔-like concept isn't in the alphabet. Let me try pointing at eyes/mark concept: I'll gesture "☝" (describe) plus "✍" (writing/marking) to suggest "describe the mark".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Still no instruction received. If you can hear me, please speak the wire number to cut, using color: yellow is wire one, green is wire two, red is wire three.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot read the plate engraving as text, but let me describe its shape. Still waiting on your answer: is wire two, green, the one to cut?

Deaf hasn't described the shape yet, still waiting for my yes/no. I need to push again for the shape description since I genuinely don't know which mark it is. Let me be very explicit with a repeated request gesture, and hold off answering yes/no since a wrong guess could be fatal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```
